verses.1: I say that, as long as the heir is a minor, there is no difference between a slave and a master in any way.
verses.2: But it is also subject to arbitrary rules and regulations up to the time of the father’s death.
verses.3: In the same way, when we were children, we were also subjected to the influence of the elements of the world.
verses.4: And when the time came for him to be born, God sent his son into the world. He was born from a woman, and he became subject to the laws of nature.
verses.5: In order to get those who are under law out of there, so that we can receive the inheritance.
verses.6: Since we are sons, the God has sent the spirit of his Son into our hearts. Abba, Father.
verses.7: So that he is no longer a slave, but a son. And if he is a son, then he is also a heir by God’s will.
verses.8: But at that time, not knowing that there was a god, they worshipped those things that aren’t actually gods at all.
verses.9: Now that you know about God, and now that you’ve been truly known by God, how can you still return to those weak and poor elements? How can you still want to serve them from above?
verses.10: You will observe days, months, years, and even decades.
verses.11: I fear that I may have spoken too harshly to you.
verses.12: Be like me, for I also, as you do, brothers, require of you. You have not given me anything.
verses.13: And you know that, due to the weakness of my flesh, I was unable to convey to you what I wanted to say earlier.
verses.14: And you did not destroy the temptation in my flesh; instead, you trusted me as a messenger of God, as Jesus Christ.
verses.15: What kind of happiness is this for you? I testify to you that if it were possible to remove your eyes from them, you would do so.
verses.16: So that he could become your enemy and thus deceive you.
verses.17: They want to make you feel inferior, not to say that they truly do that, but they want to make you look down on them.
verses.18: It’s good to be greedy for everything that’s good, and not only in matters related to our appearance before you.
verses.19: My sons, I still call upon you until Christ is formed among you.
verses.20: I would like to come before you, and change my voice, as I am being interrupted by you.
verses.21: Tell me, those who want to be under the law, don’t you obey the law?
verses.22: It is written that Abraham had two sons: one from his wife Sarah, and one from his concubine.
verses.23: But one is born from the womb of a mother, through physical birth; the other is born from freedom, through divine revelation.
verses.24: It’s the same thing we’re talking about. Both of them belong to two different people. One was born in Mount Sinna, and she became a slave. The other person was from Hagar.
verses.25: Mount Hagar Sinna is located in Arabia. It is part of what we now call Jerusalem. It is actually used as a place of worship by her descendants.
verses.26: And the upper Jerusalem is free; it is our mother.
verses.27: It is written thus: “Be happy, for she was not a woman who could be compared to others; she was not one who would be praised or admired. For many of the daughters of the desert are more desirable than those who listen to men.”
verses.28: But you, brothers, are the descendants of Ishmael’s message.
verses.29: But just as that person who was born of the flesh despised those who were born of the spirit, so too do we today.
verses.30: But what does the law say? She was forced to give up her child and her son, for the son of the child could not inherit from the son of the free woman.
verses.31: Therefore, brothers, they are not merely children of a teacher, but those of the free people.
